title: Introduce TFState migrator and shared IAM attachment for GPU subpools
author: Anya Patel
description: Motivation: Private deployments using per-cluster terraform state have become brittle during operator-driven GPU subpool rotations and cross-VPC upgrades. This PR introduces a small, opinionated tfstate-migrator tool plus a shared iam-attachment module to centralize IAM bindings for GPU node pools and to migrate legacy per-cluster state to a per-vpc + per-subpool layout. Changes include a non-destructive migration plan that creates new workspaces, moves resources, and updates remote state backends with locking and verification. Checklist: 1) add tfstate-migrator binary + docs; 2) add modules/iam/attachment to consolidate service-account-to-node-role bindings; 3) split modules/gpu-pool into pool-core + pool-node (state boundary changes); 4) update workspace naming conventions and CI plans; 5) add integration test that performs a dry-run migration on sample state. Related Linear: ENG-4981 (state migration requirements), ENG-5120 (gpu pool IAM consolidation). This PR is intended to be safe-by-default: migration runs as a distinct step and does not auto-delete resources. See migration_instructions field for step-by-step guidance.

review_comments: Marco: Can the migrator perform a no-op verify step that compares resource counts before rename? Author: added a verify mode and tests.
Lisa: IAM consolidation looks good but we need explicit lifecycle prevent_destroy for node roles. Author: added lifecycle blocks and notes in README.
Ravi: CI matrix initially flaked on backend rename lock contention; resolved by serializing workspace rename in the migrator. Author: fixed and added retry logic.
release_notes: Add tfstate-migrator CLI and shared iam-attachment module. Provides safe migration path from per-cluster state to per-vpc+subpool state and consolidates GPU node-pool IAM bindings.
changed_areas: shared IAM module for node roles/service accounts
CI workflows and migration integration tests
migration_instructions: 1) Checkout branch and run make build-migrator to build scripts/tfstate-migrator; 2) Run ./bin/tfstate-migrator --source-workspace=legacy-prod --target-prefix=vpc-1234 --dry-run and inspect the plan JSON; 3) Create target workspaces (terraform workspace new vpc-1234-subpool-a) or let migrator create them with --create-workspaces; 4) Re-run without --dry-run to perform state move; 5) Update remote backend pointers in modules that consumed legacy state; 6) Run terraform plan in each target workspace and verify no unexpected destroys; 7) Rollback instructions: use migrator --rollback-to=backup-key and follow printed restore steps. Note: migrator acquires backend locks and will abort on contention.
